Medieval Asia, in chronological order.Sui reunifies China: The Sui dynasty ended almost 400 years of division in China and built the Grand Canal, a waterway that later carried grain across the empire.
Medieval Asia, in chronological order.Taika Reform in Japan: This sweeping Japanese reform copied Tang China's model, claiming all land for the emperor and building a centralised, bureaucratic state.
Medieval Asia, in chronological order.Silla unifies Korea: With help from Tang China, the Silla kingdom defeated its rivals Baekje and Goguryeo, creating a single Korean state for the first time.
Medieval Asia, in chronological order.An Lushan Rebellion: A general's revolt nearly toppled the Tang dynasty. It cost millions of lives and weakened China's central rule for generations.
Medieval Asia, in chronological order.Khmer Empire founded: Jayavarman II launched the empire that would build Angkor Wat, the largest religious monument in the world.
Medieval Asia, in chronological order.Pagan Kingdom founded: Anawrahta founded this Burmese kingdom and spread Theravada Buddhism. Its capital became famous for thousands of temples still scattered across the plains.
Medieval Asia, in chronological order.Goryeo founded: Wang Geon founded this dynasty, and Korea's English name comes from it. It also developed early movable metal type printing.
Medieval Asia, in chronological order.Majapahit founded: This Javanese empire once dominated much of maritime Southeast Asia. Its name still turns up in Indonesia's national memory and symbols.
Medieval Asia, in chronological order.Ayutthaya founded: Named after a city in India, this Thai kingdom grew into one of Asia's great trading cities before Burmese forces sacked it in 1767.
Medieval Asia, in chronological order.Joseon founded: General Yi Seong-gye founded this Korean dynasty, which lasted until 1910 and created the Hangul alphabet under King Sejong.

Polygons, by number of sides.Pentagon: The Pentagon building in Virginia is shaped like one and was long the world's largest office building by floor area.
Polygons, by number of sides.Heptagon: The British 20p and 50p coins use this shape, with slightly curved sides so that they roll through vending machines.
Polygons, by number of sides.Nonagon: It is also called an enneagon, mixing Latin and Greek roots, and some Baháʼí Houses of Worship have nine sides.
Polygons, by number of sides.Hendecagon: Its name mixes Greek parts, it is also known as an undecagon, and it cannot be constructed with a ruler and compass.
Polygons, by number of sides.Dodecagon: The old British threepenny bit had twelve sides, and a clock face has twelve hours.
Polygons, by number of sides.Icosagon: The name comes from the Greek for twenty, the same root as icosahedron, the shape of 20-sided dice.
Polygons, by number of sides.Triacontagon: Its Greek name means thirty, and each interior angle in a regular one measures 168 degrees.
Polygons, by number of sides.Hectogon: It already looks almost like a circle, and Archimedes approximated pi with a 96-sided polygon.
Polygons, by number of sides.Chiliagon: Descartes used it to show that we can think about a thousand-sided figure without being able to picture it clearly.
Polygons, by number of sides.Myriagon: To the eye it is practically a circle, and philosophers use it to question whether we can truly imagine such shapes.

Record-breaking paintings at auction.Sunflowers (Van Gogh, 1987): Van Gogh painted sunflower still lifes in Arles to decorate Gauguin's room; this version's 1987 sale stunned the art world.
Record-breaking paintings at auction.Irises (Van Gogh): He painted it in 1889 at the asylum in Saint-Rémy; it was bought by Alan Bond in 1987 and now hangs in the Getty Museum.
Record-breaking paintings at auction.Portrait of Dr. Gachet: Van Gogh painted his doctor in 1890, weeks before his death; the buyer in 1990 reportedly said he wanted it cremated with him, causing outrage.
Record-breaking paintings at auction.Garçon à la pipe (Picasso): Picasso painted this portrait of a Paris boy in 1905; its 2004 sale was the first painting to top $100 million.
Record-breaking paintings at auction.The Scream (Munch): Munch made four versions of this image; the other three are in Norwegian museums, so this pastel was the only one that could be sold.
Record-breaking paintings at auction.Three Studies of Lucian Freud: Francis Bacon painted this 1969 triptych of his friend and rival Lucian Freud; its 2013 sale set a record for any artwork at the time.
Record-breaking paintings at auction.Nu couché (Modigliani): When Modigliani showed his nudes in Paris in 1917, police shut down the exhibition for indecency on its opening day.
Record-breaking paintings at auction.Les Femmes d'Alger (Picasso): Picasso made fifteen paintings reworking Delacroix's 1834 Women of Algiers; the one sold in 2015 is labelled version O.
Record-breaking paintings at auction.Shot Sage Blue Marilyn: Andy Warhol's 1964 silkscreen of Marilyn Monroe is the priciest American artwork ever sold at auction; it got its name when a performer shot a stack of Warhol's portraits.
Record-breaking paintings at auction.Salvator Mundi (da Vinci): Once dismissed as a copy and sold cheaply, it was authenticated as Leonardo's work and sold in 2017; where it now hangs is unclear.

When these toys first went on sale.Magic 8 Ball: The Magic 8 Ball was inspired by a spirit-writing device, and its answers come from a die floating in blue liquid.
When these toys first went on sale.Easy-Bake Oven: The Easy-Bake Oven originally used a light bulb to bake tiny cakes, and it was a big hit for Kenner.
When these toys first went on sale.Spirograph: Spirograph was invented by a British engineer, Denys Fisher, and its gears draw intricate looping patterns.
When these toys first went on sale.Nerf ball: The Nerf ball was invented by Parker Brothers, and it was originally a soft foam ball for indoor play.
When these toys first went on sale.Simon: Simon was an electronic memory game inspired by the game Simple Simon, and its four colored lights became an iconic toy.
When these toys first went on sale.Pound Puppies: Pound Puppies were stuffed dogs with a story that they came from a pound, and they led to a TV series.
When these toys first went on sale.Super Soaker: The Super Soaker was invented by NASA engineer Lonnie Johnson, who stumbled on the idea while working on a heat pump.
When these toys first went on sale.Razor scooter: The Razor scooter was a folding aluminum scooter that became a craze, and it sold millions in a short time.
When these toys first went on sale.Bakugan: Bakugan are marbles that pop open into monsters when they hit magnets, and they were a big hit alongside a TV series.
When these toys first went on sale.Hatchimals: Hatchimals are toys that hatch from eggs, and they were a hard-to-find hit during the 2016 holiday season.

From wasps to whales: who weighs more?.Common wasp: Colonies are run by one queen, who starts a new nest by herself each spring, and workers are all her daughters.
From wasps to whales: who weighs more?.House sparrow: Native to Eurasia, it spread around the world alongside people, though its numbers have dropped sharply in parts of Britain.
From wasps to whales: who weighs more?.Gray squirrel: Introduced to Britain in the 1870s, it has outcompeted the native red squirrel across much of the country.
From wasps to whales: who weighs more?.House cat: Cats sleep for roughly 12 to 16 hours a day, so a small predator spends much of its life resting.
From wasps to whales: who weighs more?.Human: Our brains weigh only around 2 percent of our body weight but burn about 20 percent of our energy.
From wasps to whales: who weighs more?.Grizzly bear: Despite their bulk, they can sprint at over 50 km/h, faster than any person.
From wasps to whales: who weighs more?.Walrus: Its tusks are enlarged canine teeth, and its scientific name, Odobenus, means tooth-walker.
From wasps to whales: who weighs more?.Orca: Technically the largest member of the dolphin family, it hunts in family pods and is also called the killer whale.
From wasps to whales: who weighs more?.Humpback whale: Males sing long, complex songs that can last for many minutes, and these songs spread across entire oceans.
From wasps to whales: who weighs more?.Fin whale: The second-largest animal ever known, it is so fast and sleek that it's nicknamed the greyhound of the sea.

Swedish companies, by founding year.Hasselblad: The Moon landing cameras were his, and the astronauts left most of the bodies behind to save weight.
Swedish companies, by founding year.Ericsson: Founder Lars Magnus Ericsson began by repairing telegraphs, and the company grew into a telecom giant.
Swedish companies, by founding year.Scania: The griffin on its trucks comes from the coat of arms of the province Skane.
Swedish companies, by founding year.Electrolux: It began with a vacuum cleaner and refrigerator, built under Axel Wenner-Gren.
Swedish companies, by founding year.Saab: The name stands for Svenska Aeroplan AB, so the company made fighter jets before it made cars.
Swedish companies, by founding year.IKEA: Its name combines founder Ingvar Kamprad's initials with Elmtaryd, the farm, and Agunnaryd, his village.
Swedish companies, by founding year.H&M: It started in Vasteras as Hennes, which means hers in Swedish, selling only women's clothing.
Swedish companies, by founding year.Tetra Pak: The company began with a tetrahedron-shaped carton for milk, invented by Ruben Rausing's team.
Swedish companies, by founding year.Oatly: The oat-milk brand began in the university city of Lund, and its drink was first meant for people with lactose intolerance.
Swedish companies, by founding year.Klarna: The buy-now-pay-later company is based in Stockholm.

Songs that came with a dance craze.The Twist: Chubby Checker's cover made it the only song to reach number one in the US in two separate runs, in 1960 and 1962.
Songs that came with a dance craze.The Loco-Motion: Little Eva, who was Carole King's babysitter, sang it, and Grand Funk and Kylie Minogue later took it back up the charts.
The Village People's anthem inspired a dance spelling out the letters with your arms, now a fixture at weddings and stadiums.
Songs that came with a dance craze.Thriller: Michael Jackson's roughly 14-minute video, directed by John Landis, made zombie dancing a pop phenomenon.
Songs that came with a dance craze.Vogue: Madonna borrowed the posing dance of Harlem's ballroom scene and carried it into the mainstream.
Songs that came with a dance craze.Macarena: Los del Rio's song spent 14 weeks at number one on the US Hot 100 in 1996.
Songs that came with a dance craze.Cha Cha Slide: DJ Casper's song is basically spoken dance instructions, made for a Chicago fitness instructor.
Songs that came with a dance craze.Crank That (Soulja Boy): Soulja Boy was a teenager when he shared it online, and its viral rise came before such things were common.
Songs that came with a dance craze.Gangnam Style: Psy's video became the first on YouTube to pass a billion views, in December 2012.
Songs that came with a dance craze.Watch Me (Whip/Nae Nae): Silento's song popularised two existing dance moves, turning them into a school playground craze.

Nature's rhythms, from a flash to an epo.Lightning flash: A flash is built from several strokes, each lasting microseconds, and its channel is briefly hotter than the Sun's surface, around 30,000 degrees Celsius.
Nature's rhythms, from a flash to an epo.Old Faithful eruption: The Yellowstone geyser erupts roughly every 90 minutes and shoots water 30 to 55 m high, and rangers predict the next eruption within a few minutes.
Nature's rhythms, from a flash to an epo.High tide to high tide: Tides arrive about 12 h 25 min apart because the Moon moves on in its orbit while Earth spins, so each lunar day is about 24 h 50 min.
Nature's rhythms, from a flash to an epo.One spin of the Earth: Measured against the stars, one real spin takes just 23 hours 56 minutes; the extra four minutes make a full solar day, because Earth also moves around the Sun.
Nature's rhythms, from a flash to an epo.Lunar month: The cycle of lunar phases, the synodic month, is about 29.5 days, longer than the Moon's 27.3-day orbit, because Earth moves around the Sun in the meantime.
Nature's rhythms, from a flash to an epo.Earth's orbit: Leap years exist because the orbit takes about 365.25 days, and the Gregorian calendar skips three leap years every 400 years to keep seasons aligned.
Nature's rhythms, from a flash to an epo.Sunspot cycle: The Sun's magnetic activity peaks about every 11 years, bringing more flares and brighter auroras, which can disrupt satellites and power grids.
Nature's rhythms, from a flash to an epo.Some bamboo's mass flowering: Some bamboo species flower all at once after roughly 120 years and then die, which can set off rat population booms and food shortages.
Nature's rhythms, from a flash to an epo.Wobble of Earth's axis: This slow wobble, called precession, shifts which star is the pole star over millennia; Polaris will give way to others, and Vega held the role in the distant past.
Nature's rhythms, from a flash to an epo.Earth's orbit stretch cycle: Slight changes in the orbit's shape, called eccentricity, are one of the Milankovitch cycles that scientists link to the timing of the ice ages.

When these beers were first brewed.Guinness: Arthur Guinness signed a 9,000-year lease on his Dublin brewery, at an annual rent of 45 pounds, and its dark stout became Ireland's icon.
When these beers were first brewed.Pilsner Urquell: The world's first golden lager was brewed in Plzen, in what is now Czechia, and it inspired most pale lagers made since.
When these beers were first brewed.Carlsberg: Founded by J.C. Jacobsen and named for his son Carl, this Danish brewery funded science and its labs discovered the pH scale.
When these beers were first brewed.Heineken: The Dutch brand's red star logo is a famous symbol, and its founder's grandson Freddy Heineken was once kidnapped for ransom in 1983.
When these beers were first brewed.Budweiser: Adolphus Busch introduced this US lager inspired by the Czech town of Budweis, and it was the first national beer brand in the US.
When these beers were first brewed.Tsingtao: China's best-known beer began in Qingdao, then a German colony, and it is often served in a plastic bag in the city's streets.
When these beers were first brewed.Corona: The Mexican lager, often served with a lime wedge, is Mexico's best-selling export beer, and it is sold in clear bottles, which are prone to light damage.
When these beers were first brewed.Sierra Nevada: The California brewery's Pale Ale helped make craft beer popular, and it was among the first to popularize the Cascade hop.
When these beers were first brewed.Samuel Adams: Named for the American Revolution firebrand, this Boston lager made by Jim Koch launched in 1984 using a family recipe from his great-great-grandfather.
When these beers were first brewed.BrewDog: A Scottish craft brewery founded by two friends, it grew by selling its beers with cheeky names, and its founders were just in their twenties.

The school reading list, by publication.The Odyssey: The Odyssey is thought to have been composed around the 8th century BC, and it was passed on by memory before it was written down.
The school reading list, by publication.Romeo and Juliet: Romeo and Juliet was written in the 1590s, and its two lovers are teenagers, and Juliet is only about 13.
The school reading list, by publication.The Scarlet Letter: The Scarlet Letter, by Nathaniel Hawthorne, follows a woman forced to wear a red 'A' for adultery in Puritan Boston.
The school reading list, by publication.Adventures of Huckleberry Finn: Mark Twain's Huckleberry Finn was banned in some places, and is often called the Great American Novel.
The school reading list, by publication.The Great Gatsby: The Great Gatsby sold poorly at first, and Fitzgerald died believing it was a failure.
The school reading list, by publication.Of Mice and Men: Of Mice and Men, by John Steinbeck, takes its title from a Robert Burns poem, and is one of the most challenged books in America.
The school reading list, by publication.Animal Farm: Animal Farm was rejected by several publishers, and George Orwell wrote it as a satire of the Russian Revolution.
The school reading list, by publication.Lord of the Flies: Lord of the Flies, William Golding's novel about boys stranded on an island, was rejected by many publishers before success.
The school reading list, by publication.To Kill a Mockingbird: To Kill a Mockingbird by Harper Lee won the Pulitzer Prize, and was her only novel for over 50 years until Go Set a Watchman.
The school reading list, by publication.The Giver: The Giver, by Lois Lowry, won the Newbery Medal, and is set in a society where all pain and color has been removed.

Business and style publications, by foun.The Economist: Founded by James Wilson to campaign against the Corn Laws. Its articles are unsigned, and it calls itself a newspaper.
Business and style publications, by foun.The Wall Street Journal: Started by Dow Jones & Co. as a small afternoon paper; Charles Dow also created the Dow Jones average.
Business and style publications, by foun.Vogue: It began as a weekly for New York high society, and Conde Nast bought it in 1909.
Business and style publications, by foun.Forbes: Founded by B. C. Forbes, a Scottish immigrant. Its rich lists, like the Forbes 400, started in 1982.
Business and style publications, by foun.Time: Henry Luce and Briton Hadden's magazine was the first US weekly news magazine, and its red border is famous.
Business and style publications, by foun.BusinessWeek: It launched just before the 1929 stock market crash. Bloomberg bought it in 2009.
Business and style publications, by foun.Rolling Stone: Founded in San Francisco by Jann Wenner and Ralph Gleason; its name nods to a Muddy Waters song.
Business and style publications, by foun.Bloomberg: Michael Bloomberg founded the company around its terminal, a data machine that traders still depend on.
Business and style publications, by foun.Wired: It launched in San Francisco in 1993, when the Web was barely public, and chronicled the digital revolution.
Business and style publications, by foun.Business Insider: Henry Blodget founded it as Silicon Alley Insider, and Axel Springer bought it in 2015.

Periods of Japanese history.Jomon: Its name means cord-marked, after its pottery, some of the world's oldest, made about 14,000 years ago.
Periods of Japanese history.Yayoi: Brought rice farming and metalworking from the Asian mainland.
Periods of Japanese history.Kofun: Named for its huge keyhole-shaped burial mounds, one of which, Daisen, is the largest tomb on earth by area.
Periods of Japanese history.Asuka: Buddhism was formally introduced in 538, and Prince Shotoku later helped shape the state.
Periods of Japanese history.Nara: Japan's first permanent capital, Heijo-kyo, was founded in 710, and Todai-ji's Great Buddha was cast here.
Periods of Japanese history.Heian: The capital was Kyoto, and Murasaki Shikibu wrote The Tale of Genji, often called the world's first novel.
Periods of Japanese history.Kamakura: Samurai rule began with the first shogun, Minamoto no Yoritomo, and defenses repelled Mongol invasions in 1274 and 1281.
Periods of Japanese history.Muromachi: Ashikaga shoguns ruled; Zen gardens and Noh theater flourished, though the Onin War led to a century of conflict.
Periods of Japanese history.Edo: Tokugawa shoguns brought about 250 years of peace and isolation. Edo is now called Tokyo.
Periods of Japanese history.Meiji: The emperor was restored to power and Japan modernized with astonishing speed, ending the samurai class.

PlayStation hardware by release.PlayStation: Born from a failed deal with Nintendo for a Super Nintendo CD add-on, driven by Sony engineer Ken Kutaragi.
PlayStation hardware by release.PocketStation: A Japan-only memory card with a small LCD screen, it ran mini-games and looked ahead to portable consoles.
PlayStation hardware by release.PlayStation 2: The best-selling home console of all time, with over 150 million sold, and it also served as a cheap DVD player in many homes.
PlayStation hardware by release.PSP: Its games came on UMD, a Sony disc format that never took off, but the system was the first handheld with console-like 3D power.
PlayStation hardware by release.PlayStation 3: Its Cell processor was famously hard to program, and its built-in Blu-ray drive helped Blu-ray win the format war with HD DVD.
PlayStation hardware by release.PS Vita: Its OLED screen and rear touchpad were ahead of their time, and it never matched Nintendo's 3DS in sales but has loyal fans.
PlayStation hardware by release.PlayStation 4: It sold over 100 million units, with a clear lead over the Xbox One in the console generation that began in 2013.
PlayStation hardware by release.PlayStation VR: The headset was tracked by a camera watching lights on its surface, and it needed a PS4 to work.
PlayStation hardware by release.PlayStation 5: Famed for a super-fast SSD and a DualSense controller with haptic feedback and adaptive triggers, it launched into a global supply shortage.
PlayStation hardware by release.PlayStation Portal: A handheld that streams PS5 games over Wi-Fi but cannot run them itself, so it is useless without a PS5 nearby.

Everyday health breakthroughs.Aspirin: Bayer began selling it in 1899; its active ingredient descends from compounds in willow bark, long used for pain.
Everyday health breakthroughs.Chlorinated tap water: Jersey City began chlorinating in 1908, sharply cutting typhoid and cholera, one of public health's biggest wins.
Everyday health breakthroughs.Band-Aid: Earle Dickson invented it for his accident-prone wife, and his employer Johnson & Johnson began selling it.
Everyday health breakthroughs.Iodized salt: Introduced in the US in 1924 to prevent goiter, which had been common in inland areas short on dietary iodine.
Everyday health breakthroughs.Water fluoridation: Grand Rapids, Michigan, was the first city to add fluoride to its water, aiming to cut tooth decay.
Everyday health breakthroughs.Tylenol: Launched in 1955 as a children's medicine, it contains paracetamol, known as acetaminophen in the US.
Everyday health breakthroughs.Modern CPR: Combining chest compressions and rescue breaths was shown in 1960; the beat of 'Stayin' Alive' is a popular pace guide.
Everyday health breakthroughs.Ibuprofen launched: Developed by researchers at Boots in Nottingham, it first reached patients in the UK as a prescription anti-inflammatory.
Everyday health breakthroughs.Heimlich maneuver: It's named after the American doctor who described abdominal thrusts for clearing a blocked airway.
Everyday health breakthroughs.Nicotine patch: Approved in the US in 1991 as a smoking-cessation aid, it delivers nicotine steadily through the skin.

Heavyweight champions, by first title.Jack Johnson: In Sydney in 1908 he became the first Black world heavyweight champion, defeating Tommy Burns.
Heavyweight champions, by first title.Jack Dempsey: The 'Manassa Mauler' headlined boxing's first million-dollar gate against Georges Carpentier in 1921.
Heavyweight champions, by first title.Joe Louis: The 'Brown Bomber' held the title for over 11 years, with a record 25 successful defenses.
Heavyweight champions, by first title.Rocky Marciano: He retired in 1956 with an unbeaten 49-0 record, which no heavyweight champion has beaten.
Heavyweight champions, by first title.Floyd Patterson: At 21 he was then the youngest heavyweight champion and later the first to regain the title.
Heavyweight champions, by first title.Muhammad Ali (as Cassius Clay): He shocked Sonny Liston, then announced he'd joined the Nation of Islam and took the name Muhammad Ali.
Heavyweight champions, by first title.George Foreman: He knocked out Joe Frazier to win the crown, and regained it at 45 in 1994, the oldest heavyweight champion.
Heavyweight champions, by first title.Larry Holmes: He defended his title 20 times, and his 48 straight wins fell one short of Marciano's mark.
Heavyweight champions, by first title.Mike Tyson: At 20 he became the youngest heavyweight champion in history, before his later fall from the top.
Heavyweight champions, by first title.Evander Holyfield: A four-time heavyweight champion, he's the only boxer to win the heavyweight title four times.

When these spirit brands were founded.Gordon's gin: The London dry gin, started by Alexander Gordon in 1769, is sold in green bottles, and its recipe has been kept secret since.
When these spirit brands were founded.Jose Cuervo: One of the oldest tequila brands, from Jalisco, Mexico, was founded in 1795 and named for the Cuervo family, which holds the oldest tequila license.
When these spirit brands were founded.Tanqueray: Charles Tanqueray launched it in London in 1830, and its distinctive green bottle is often said to be modeled on a cocktail shaker.
When these spirit brands were founded.Bacardi: Founded in Santiago de Cuba in 1862, it's known for its bat logo, which is believed to bring good luck, since fruit bats lived in the distillery's rafters.
When these spirit brands were founded.Aperol: This bright orange Italian aperitif, created in Padua, is the key to the Aperol Spritz, which became hugely popular in the 21st century.
When these spirit brands were founded.Kahlúa: This coffee liqueur from Veracruz, Mexico, is the main ingredient of the White Russian, a drink made famous by the film The Big Lebowski.
When these spirit brands were founded.Captain Morgan: This rum is named for a Welsh pirate who became lieutenant governor of Jamaica, and its mascot's pose, with one foot on a cask, is famous.
When these spirit brands were founded.Baileys: Irish cream liqueur created in Dublin in 1974, mixing Irish whiskey with cream, and one of the world's best-selling liqueurs.
When these spirit brands were founded.Patrón: A premium tequila brand launched in 1989. Its name is Spanish for "boss" or "patron", and its bottles are handmade.
When these spirit brands were founded.Grey Goose: French vodka brand created in 1997 by Sidney Frank, it was sold to Bacardi in 2004 for $2 billion, one of the largest spirit deals.

Natural lifespans, from a day to centuri.Adult mayfly: Adult mayflies often have no working mouth, and they live only long enough to mate; the order's name means short-lived.
Natural lifespans, from a day to centuri.Summer worker honeybee: A summer worker bee works herself to death in about six weeks, while winter bees can live months.
Natural lifespans, from a day to centuri.Golden hamster: Golden hamsters were found in Syria in 1930, and today's pets descend from just a handful of ancestors.
Natural lifespans, from a day to centuri.Guinea pig: Guinea pigs can't make their own vitamin C, just like humans, and they're social animals that need company.
Natural lifespans, from a day to centuri.House cat: Cats sleep about two-thirds of the day, and indoor ones tend to live much longer than outdoor cats.
Natural lifespans, from a day to centuri.Horse: Horses can sleep standing up thanks to a locking mechanism in their legs.
Natural lifespans, from a day to centuri.African elephant: African elephants can live as long as people, and the oldest female leads the family herd.
Natural lifespans, from a day to centuri.Galápagos tortoise: Galápagos tortoises can survive a year without food or water, and some captive ones have been recorded living beyond 150 years.
Natural lifespans, from a day to centuri.Bowhead whale: Bowhead whales can break through ice with their heads, and their long lives may come from unusually effective DNA repair.
Natural lifespans, from a day to centuri.Greenland shark: The Greenland shark may live up to about 400 years, growing only a centimeter per year, and it reaches maturity at around 150.

Legendary sporting moments.Babe Ruth hits 60 homers: It broke a record that stood until Roger Maris hit 61 in 1961, a feat debated because of the longer season.
Legendary sporting moments.Owens wins 4 golds in Berlin: His four golds in Berlin, in front of Hitler, were in the 100 m, 200 m, long jump and 4x100 relay.
Legendary sporting moments.Jackie Robinson's MLB debut: He broke baseball's colour line on 15 April, and his number 42 is retired across the entire league.
Legendary sporting moments.Bannister's sub-4 mile: He ran 3:59.4 at Oxford, and his record lasted only 46 days before John Landy beat it.
Legendary sporting moments.Wilt scores 100 in a game: It was scored on 2 March in Hershey, Pennsylvania, with no video; the game was not even televised.
Legendary sporting moments.Bob Beamon's huge long jump: His 8.90 m jump in Mexico City's thin air beat the record by 55 cm and stood for 23 years.
Legendary sporting moments.Hank Aaron's 715th homer: On 8 April he passed Babe Ruth's 714, and he faced racist threats during the chase.
Legendary sporting moments.Comaneci's perfect 10: She scored it on the uneven bars at age 14; the scoreboard could not show 10.00, so it displayed 1.00.
Legendary sporting moments.Miracle on Ice: US college players beat the Soviets at Lake Placid; Al Michaels asked, 'Do you believe in miracles?'
Legendary sporting moments.Deep Blue beats Kasparov: It was the first time a computer beat a reigning world champion in a match under standard chess tournament conditions.

When these invented languages were creat.Lingua Ignota (Hildegard): The medieval abbess Hildegard of Bingen devised this 'unknown language' of about a thousand words, known today only from a glossary and her songs.
When these invented languages were creat.Volapük: Priest Johann Martin Schleyer created it in Germany, and it briefly had hundreds of clubs before Esperanto overshadowed it.
When these invented languages were creat.Esperanto: L. L. Zamenhof published it as 'Doktoro Esperanto', the pen name that became its title. It is still the most widely spoken invented language.
When these invented languages were creat.Quenya (Tolkien's Elvish): Tolkien built it partly on Finnish and often said his stories grew out of his languages, not the other way round.
When these invented languages were creat.Newspeak: Orwell's language in 1984 shrinks vocabulary so rebellious thoughts become impossible to express, and its name is now shorthand for political doublespeak.
When these invented languages were creat.Nadsat (A Clockwork Orange): Anthony Burgess's teen slang leans on Russian: 'droog' means friend, and 'horrorshow' comes from 'khorosho', meaning good.
When these invented languages were creat.Klingon: Linguist Marc Okrand built it for Star Trek, and its sentences run object-verb-subject. Fans have translated Shakespeare into it.
When these invented languages were creat.Lojban: Designed to be free of ambiguity so that computers can parse it, its name comes from 'logical language'. It grew out of an earlier project called Loglan.
When these invented languages were creat.Toki Pona: Sonja Lang's language has only around 120 to 140 words. Its name means 'good language', and it is meant to encourage simple thinking.
When these invented languages were creat.Dothraki: David J. Peterson won HBO's contest to build it for Game of Thrones, drawing on real languages such as Russian and Swahili.

When these modern states were born.Dutch Republic: Dutch rebels declared independence from Spain in 1581 and the republic became a trading power in its Golden Age.
When these modern states were born.Kingdom of Great Britain: The Acts of Union joined England and Scotland, creating the flag known as the Union Jack, and it lasted until Ireland was added in 1801.
When these modern states were born.United States: The Declaration of Independence was adopted on July 4, and it was mainly written by Thomas Jefferson, then only 33.
When these modern states were born.Kingdom of Italy: The country's unification under King Victor Emmanuel II came after Garibaldi's campaigns, and Rome only joined in 1871.
When these modern states were born.Canada (Confederation): Canada was formed from three colonies with only about 3.5 million people, and Ottawa was chosen as capital by Queen Victoria.
When these modern states were born.German Empire: Germany unified after victory over France, and Wilhelm I was proclaimed emperor in the Hall of Mirrors at Versailles.
When these modern states were born.Commonwealth of Australia: Six colonies federated into a country, and the new capital, Canberra, was chosen in a compromise between Sydney and Melbourne.
When these modern states were born.Republic of Turkey: Mustafa Kemal Atatürk founded the republic after the fall of the Ottoman Empire, and he introduced the Latin alphabet and surnames.
When these modern states were born.People's Republic of China: Mao Zedong proclaimed it in Tiananmen Square after the civil war, and the nation is now home to over a billion people.
When these modern states were born.Singapore: The city-state became independent after leaving Malaysia, and Lee Kuan Yew led it from a poor port to a wealthy financial hub.

The Fast & Furious saga by release.The Fast and the Furious: The first film introduced street racing and a young undercover cop played by Paul Walker, and it was based on a magazine article.
The Fast & Furious saga by release.2 Fast 2 Furious: The sequel brought in Tyrese Gibson and Ludacris, and it was set in Miami, with Paul Walker returning without Vin Diesel.
The Fast & Furious saga by release.Tokyo Drift: The film is set in Japan, and its lead is a teenager sent to live with his father, and it was filmed in Tokyo, with drifting.
The Fast & Furious saga by release.Fast & Furious (the 4th): The fourth film reunited the original cast, and it began a new phase of the series, with a more heist-oriented plot.
The Fast & Furious saga by release.Fast Five: The heist in Rio is the highlight, with a vault dragged through the streets, and The Rock joined the series.
The Fast & Furious saga by release.Fast & Furious 6: The film ends with a very long runway, and the length was said to be about 28 miles, and it was said to be the longest runway of all time.
The Fast & Furious saga by release.Furious 7: It was Paul Walker's last film, and his brothers helped complete his scenes, and it ended with a tribute to him.
The Fast & Furious saga by release.The Fate of the Furious: The film includes a scene with cars falling from a parking garage, and it was set in New York, Cuba and Russia.
The Fast & Furious saga by release.F9: The ninth main film sent the crew into space in a car with a rocket, and it was delayed by the pandemic.
The Fast & Furious saga by release.Fast X: The tenth film is the first of a planned two-part finale, and it features Jason Momoa as a villain.

Counting pieces in board games.Chinese checkers marbles each: Despite the name it came from Germany, as a star-shaped variant of Halma called Stern-Halma, and was renamed in the 1920s.
Counting pieces in board games.Checkers per side: Called draughts in Britain, it was proved in 2007 to be a draw with perfect play, by a long computer calculation.
Counting pieces in board games.Backgammon checkers per side: This descendant of ancient race games of the Near East is some 5,000 years old, and the doubling cube arrived only in the 1920s.
Counting pieces in board games.Xiangqi pieces per side: Chinese chess has a river across the middle of the board and a palace that confines the general.
Counting pieces in board games.Shogi pieces per side: Captured pieces here can be dropped back on the board by the captor, a rule unique among major chess variants.
Counting pieces in board games.Tiles in double-six dominoes: A double-six set has 28 tiles, and the game likely came from China.
Counting pieces in board games.Pieces per Stratego army: Pieces face away so their ranks stay hidden, and only the lowly spy can beat the top-ranked Marshal, if it strikes first.
Counting pieces in board games.Tiles in English Scrabble: Architect Alfred Butts invented it during the Great Depression, first calling it Lexiko, then Criss-Crosswords.
Counting pieces in board games.Mahjong tiles (with flowers): Sets come with 144 tiles including flowers and seasons, and it was a huge craze in 1920s America.
Counting pieces in board games.Black stones in a Go set: A full set has 181 black and 180 white stones, and Go has more possible positions than atoms in the observable universe.

Birthstones through the calendar year.Garnet: The name comes from Latin granatus, pomegranate, because its small red grains resemble the fruit's seeds.
Birthstones through the calendar year.Amethyst: The name is Greek for not intoxicated, because it was once believed to prevent drunkenness.
Birthstones through the calendar year.Aquamarine: The name means seawater in Latin, and sailors carried it for luck on voyages.
Birthstones through the calendar year.Diamond: Pure carbon forged about 150 km deep in the Earth, it is the hardest natural material and is brought up by volcanic eruptions.
Birthstones through the calendar year.Emerald: Cleopatra loved them, and its cloudy internal flaws are called the jardin, French for garden.
Birthstones through the calendar year.Ruby: The red variety of the mineral corundum, which makes it the same stone as sapphire with different trace elements.
Birthstones through the calendar year.Peridot: The gem form of olivine, it is found even in meteorites, and in the green sand of some Hawaiian beaches.
Birthstones through the calendar year.Sapphire: Corundum of any color except red, and most famous in blue, the color created by traces of iron and titanium.
Birthstones through the calendar year.Opal: It contains up to about 20% water, and its play of color comes from tiny silica spheres that diffract light.
Birthstones through the calendar year.Turquoise: The name means Turkish in French, since the stone reached Europe through Turkey, and Egypt mined it millennia ago.

Famous golf courses, by founding.St Andrews Old Course: The Old Course set the standard of 18 holes when it cut its layout from 22 in the 1760s.
Famous golf courses, by founding.Prestwick: It hosted the first Open Championship in 1860, when it had only twelve holes.
Famous golf courses, by founding.Royal Troon: The 8th hole is called the Postage Stamp for its tiny green and is among the shortest in championship golf.
Famous golf courses, by founding.Shinnecock Hills: One of the five founding clubs of the USGA, it also has a clubhouse designed by Stanford White.
Famous golf courses, by founding.Oakmont: It has hosted more US Opens than any other course and is known for its church pew bunkers.
Famous golf courses, by founding.Pinehurst No. 2: Donald Ross designed it with greens shaped like upturned saucers, which send balls rolling off.
Famous golf courses, by founding.Pebble Beach: It sits on the California coastline and hosts the AT&T Pro-Am, started by Bing Crosby.
Famous golf courses, by founding.Augusta National: The home of the Masters was a plant nursery, and each hole is named after a tree or flower.
Famous golf courses, by founding.Bethpage Black: This public course in New York State has a sign warning golfers that it is extremely difficult.
Famous golf courses, by founding.TPC Sawgrass: Its 17th hole is a famous green on an island, and it hosts the Players Championship.

Pressures from thin air to the Sun's cor.Surface of Mars: The air pressure is under 1% of Earth's, so liquid water cannot persist on the surface for long.
Pressures from thin air to the Sun's cor.Summit of Everest: At the top of the world there's about a third of sea-level pressure, which is why climbers carry oxygen.
Pressures from thin air to the Sun's cor.Sea level: Standard atmospheric pressure is 101.3 kPa, or 14.7 psi; each square centimetre carries about a kilogram of air.
Pressures from thin air to the Sun's cor.Inside a champagne bottle: Champagne's pressure is about three times a car tyre's, and a cork can fly out at around 50 km/h.
Pressures from thin air to the Sun's cor.Surface of Venus: Equal to being about 900 m under Earth's ocean; Soviet Venera probes survived only about two hours.
Pressures from thin air to the Sun's cor.Full scuba tank: A full tank holds roughly 200 bar and packs a couple of thousand litres of air into a small cylinder.
Pressures from thin air to the Sun's cor.Bottom of the Mariana Trench: At Challenger Deep, nearly 11 km down, the pressure is over 1,000 times that at the surface.
Pressures from thin air to the Sun's cor.Where diamonds form: Diamonds form roughly 150 km down in the mantle and ride to the surface in rare kimberlite eruptions.
Pressures from thin air to the Sun's cor.Earth's core: Pressure at Earth's center keeps the iron-nickel core solid despite temperatures around 5,000 °C.
Pressures from thin air to the Sun's cor.Sun's core: Equal to about 250 billion atmospheres, it is intense enough to fuse hydrogen into helium.

Temperatures in Fahrenheit.Ice cream, as served: Ice cream sits at about minus 13 °C, since sugar and fat lower its freezing point, which keeps it soft enough to scoop.
Temperatures in Fahrenheit.Cold beer from the fridge: Lagers are often served near this temperature; colder dulls the flavour, so ales are served warmer.
Temperatures in Fahrenheit.Room temperature: Scientists often use 20–25 °C as 'room temperature' for experiments.
Temperatures in Fahrenheit.Swimming pool: Competition pools are generally kept cooler, around 25–28 °C, to prevent overheating swimmers.
Temperatures in Fahrenheit.Body temperature: The number came from German doctor Carl Wunderlich in the 19th century; today's average is slightly lower, near 97.9 °F.
Temperatures in Fahrenheit.Sous-vide medium-rare steak: Cooking steak in a precisely heated water bath gives even doneness edge to edge; 131 °F is 55 °C.
Temperatures in Fahrenheit.Hot coffee as served: Coffee is brewed at about 195–205 °F and cools to about this when served, hot enough to scald.
Temperatures in Fahrenheit.Boiling water: Water boils at this temperature at sea level, but lower on mountains, which is why cooking takes longer at altitude.
Temperatures in Fahrenheit.Oven for baking cookies: The all-American baking default, about 175 °C, browns sugars and proteins through the Maillard reaction.
Temperatures in Fahrenheit.Broiler: A broiler heats from above using intense infrared, to brown and char food quickly.

When these candies hit the shelves.Hershey's milk chocolate bar: Milton Hershey made his fortune on caramels first; his milk chocolate bar turned chocolate from a luxury into an everyday American treat.
When these candies hit the shelves.Life Savers: Clarence Crane invented these as a summer mint, since chocolate melted in the heat; the hole gave them a lifebuoy look.
When these candies hit the shelves.Milky Way: Despite the name, it honors a malted milkshake, not the galaxy. Frank Mars wanted a candy bar that tasted like one.
When these candies hit the shelves.Reese's Peanut Butter Cups: H.B. Reese, a former Hershey employee, started these in his basement; Hershey bought his company decades later.
When these candies hit the shelves.Snickers: Mars named it after a favorite family horse, a trivia detail that surprises most people who grab one.
When these candies hit the shelves.Kit Kat: It began in York, England, as a Rowntree's wafer. In Japan it's a good-luck charm, since 'kitto katsu' sounds like 'surely win'.
When these candies hit the shelves.Starburst: Britain knew these as Opal Fruits until 1998, when the name finally switched to match the American Starburst.
When these candies hit the shelves.Twix: The name is thought to come from 'twin sticks', and the cookie-caramel-chocolate bar began in Britain, not America.
When these candies hit the shelves.Skittles: Skittles began in Britain and reached the US about five years later, with 'Taste the Rainbow' as its famous slogan.
When these candies hit the shelves.Ferrero Rocher: Ferrero's name nods to the Massabielle grotto rock at Lourdes, and each ball hides a whole hazelnut under the wafer shell.

Movie robots by their screen debut.Maria (Metropolis): Fritz Lang's film introduced the robot to cinema in 1927, with a silvery female android modeled on actress Brigitte Helm.
Movie robots by their screen debut.Robby the Robot: The towering metal servant of Forbidden Planet, Robby, was so popular that he returned in films and TV for years.
Movie robots by their screen debut.HAL 9000: The calm-voiced computer in 2001: A Space Odyssey, with a red eye, famously says 'I'm sorry, Dave, I'm afraid I can't do that.'
Movie robots by their screen debut.R2-D2: The beeping astromech droid in Star Wars was played by a short actor inside and operated by remote control.
Movie robots by their screen debut.The T-800 Terminator: Arnold Schwarzenegger's cyborg in The Terminator has few lines, and he became a hero in the sequel.
Movie robots by their screen debut.Johnny 5 (Short Circuit): A solar-powered, army-built robot struck by lightning, who gains a mind, and shouts 'Need input!'
Movie robots by their screen debut.RoboCop: A half-man, half-machine Detroit cop, the film is a satire of corporate greed, and was directed by Paul Verhoeven.
Movie robots by their screen debut.Sonny (I, Robot): Played through motion capture by Alan Tudyk, this robot in a Will Smith film is a one-of-a-kind NS-5 model.
Movie robots by their screen debut.WALL-E: Pixar's trash-compacting robot has almost no dialogue for the first half hour of its film.
Movie robots by their screen debut.Baymax: The inflatable healthcare companion of Big Hero 6 was inspired by soft robotics research at Carnegie Mellon.

Lost species: the year last seen alive.Rodrigues solitaire: A flightless relative of the dodo, it lived on Rodrigues island in the Indian Ocean until settlers and their pigs wiped it out.
Lost species: the year last seen alive.Rocky Mountain locust: Swarms in the 1870s were the biggest ever recorded, trillions of insects strong, yet the species vanished within decades.
Lost species: the year last seen alive.Desert rat-kangaroo: A small hopping marsupial of Australia's Lake Eyre basin, it was last collected in 1935, and introduced foxes and cats are blamed.
Lost species: the year last seen alive.Xerces blue butterfly: This blue butterfly lived in San Francisco's coastal dunes and is often called the first US insect driven extinct by urban sprawl.
Lost species: the year last seen alive.Tecopa pupfish: This fish lived only in hot springs near Tecopa, California, and bathhouse building plus introduced fish ended it by the 1970s.
Lost species: the year last seen alive.Round Island burrowing boa: A snake from a tiny islet near Mauritius, it had an unusual hinged upper jaw, and rabbits and goats destroyed its habitat.
Lost species: the year last seen alive.Northern gastric-brooding frog: Females of this Australian frog swallowed their fertilized eggs and raised tadpoles in the stomach, switching off the acid.
Lost species: the year last seen alive.Golden toad: The brilliant orange males gathered in the cloud forest of Monteverde, Costa Rica, and it is often cited as an early climate-linked extinction.
Lost species: the year last seen alive.Po'ouli: This Hawaiian honeycreeper was only discovered in 1973, and the last known bird died in captivity in 2004.
Lost species: the year last seen alive.Christmas Island pipistrelle: Once abundant on its island, this tiny bat was lost despite last-minute rescue attempts, and its final echolocation call was recorded in 2009.

Turning points in Irish history.Flight of the Earls: Hugh O'Neill and Rory O'Donnell sailed from Rathmullan with about 90 followers, leaving Gaelic Ulster open to English plantation.
Turning points in Irish history.Cromwell at Drogheda: Cromwell's army stormed the town after a siege and killed most of the garrison and some civilians, a massacre still bitterly remembered in Ireland.
Turning points in Irish history.Battle of the Boyne: William of Orange beat the Catholic James II here; Orange Order marches still commemorate the victory every July.
Turning points in Irish history.United Irishmen rebellion: Inspired by the American and French revolutions, Wolfe Tone's society sought to unite Catholics, Protestants and Dissenters; its failed revolt led to the 1801 Act of Union.
Turning points in Irish history.Great Famine begins: Potato blight ruined the staple crop; about a million people died and another million emigrated, cutting Ireland's population by roughly a quarter.
Turning points in Irish history.Fenian Rising: This failed rising by the Irish Republican Brotherhood took its nickname from the Fianna, the warrior bands of Irish legend.
Turning points in Irish history.Easter Rising: Rebels seized the General Post Office in Dublin on Easter Monday; the execution of their leaders turned public opinion toward independence.
Turning points in Irish history.Irish Free State founded: Born from the 1921 Anglo-Irish Treaty, this dominion split the nationalist movement and was followed at once by a bitter civil war.
Turning points in Irish history.Republic of Ireland Act: It took effect on Easter Monday 1949, cutting the last ties with the British Crown and taking Ireland out of the Commonwealth.
Turning points in Irish history.Bloody Sunday in Derry: British paratroopers shot dead 13 civil rights marchers that day (a 14th died later); the 2010 Saville Report found the killings unjustified.

Cartoon stars by their screen debut.Felix the Cat: Felix is often called the first true cartoon star, and in 1928 his figure was used for early experimental TV broadcasts.
Cartoon stars by their screen debut.Mickey Mouse: The 1928 short Steamboat Willie is the famous debut, and Walt Disney himself voiced Mickey for many years.
Cartoon stars by their screen debut.Betty Boop: She began life as a dog-like character, and singer Helen Kane sued over her baby-voiced 'boop-oop-a-doop' style.
Cartoon stars by their screen debut.Popeye (animated): The sailor was in the comics from 1929 and reached screens in Fleischer shorts, where his forearms and pipe made him instantly recognisable.
Cartoon stars by their screen debut.Porky Pig: The stuttering pig was the first big star of Looney Tunes, and in 1937 Mel Blanc took over his voice.
Cartoon stars by their screen debut.Daffy Duck: He first appeared in 1937, and Tex Avery's cartoon introduced him as a screwball, with the 'woo-hoo' that made him unforgettable.
Cartoon stars by their screen debut.Bugs Bunny: His debut 'A Wild Hare' introduced 'What's up, Doc?', and Tex Avery's rabbit was deliberately cool and unflappable.
Cartoon stars by their screen debut.Road Runner: Chuck Jones's coyote-and-bird duo followed strict rules, like no dialogue except 'Meep, meep' and the Coyote never harmed by anything but himself.
Cartoon stars by their screen debut.Yogi Bear: Debuting as a segment on The Huckleberry Hound Show, he lived in Jellystone Park and was forever stealing picnic baskets.
Cartoon stars by their screen debut.Fred Flintstone: The Flintstones was the first animated series in American prime time, and it borrowed its setup from The Honeymooners.

Ancient and medieval bridges, by age.Arkadiko Bridge, Greece: This Mycenaean bridge in the Peloponnese is built of stones fitted together without mortar, and parts of it are still in use.
Ancient and medieval bridges, by age.Ponte Fabricio, Rome: It links Rome's Tiber Island to the bank, and it's the oldest Roman bridge in the city that survives in its original form.
Ancient and medieval bridges, by age.Pont du Gard aqueduct: Built without mortar, this huge three-tier aqueduct near Nîmes rises 49 m, and it carried water to the city.
Ancient and medieval bridges, by age.Zhaozhou Bridge, China: Built by Li Chun, it is the oldest surviving open-spandrel stone arch bridge, with small arches that lighten its weight.
Ancient and medieval bridges, by age.Ponte Vecchio: Butchers once sold from its shops, until they were replaced by goldsmiths, and it was the only Florence bridge spared in WWII.
Ancient and medieval bridges, by age.Charles Bridge, Prague: Legend says egg yolks were added to the mortar for strength; it spans the Vltava and is lined with statues.
Ancient and medieval bridges, by age.Stari Most, Mostar: Its single arch was built by the Ottomans, destroyed in the 1993 war, and rebuilt using the original stone in 2004.
Ancient and medieval bridges, by age.Pont Neuf, Paris: Despite its name, the 'New Bridge' is the oldest standing bridge across the Seine in Paris.
Ancient and medieval bridges, by age.Khaju Bridge, Isfahan: This two-level Safavid bridge is also a dam and meeting place, with arched alcoves where people gather.
Ancient and medieval bridges, by age.The Iron Bridge: The first major bridge made of cast iron, in Coalbrookdale, England, it became a symbol of the Industrial Revolution.

Made in Japan: when these hits arrived.Instant ramen (Chicken Ramen): Momofuku Ando invented it in 1958 after seeing long queues at black-market noodle stalls in postwar Osaka.
Made in Japan: when these hits arrived.Pocky: The name echoes the 'pokkin' sound of the biscuit snapping, and Pocky Day is celebrated every 11 November.
Made in Japan: when these hits arrived.Cup Noodles: Ando got the idea after seeing Americans break noodles into cups, and it later even reached space on shuttle flights.
Made in Japan: when these hits arrived.Hello Kitty: Sanrio's character has no mouth, and her official biography says she is a girl named Kitty White from London.
Made in Japan: when these hits arrived.Space Invaders: A well-worn tale says it caused a shortage of 100-yen coins in Japan, though that's probably legend.
Made in Japan: when these hits arrived.Pac-Man: Namco's designer Toru Iwatani said the shape came from a pizza with a slice missing.
Made in Japan: when these hits arrived.Pokémon Red and Green: Inspired by Satoshi Tajiri's childhood bug collecting, the games launched a franchise that became the biggest in media.
Made in Japan: when these hits arrived.Emoji (NTT Docomo): Shigetaka Kurita designed 176 tiny pictures, 12 by 12 pixels, and the originals are now in New York's MoMA.
Made in Japan: when these hits arrived.Nintendo DS: With its two screens, this Nintendo handheld became one of the best-selling consoles ever.
Made in Japan: when these hits arrived.LINE messaging app: Created after the 2011 earthquake, it became hugely popular in Japan, Thailand and Taiwan.

Christopher Nolan films by release.Following: Shot on about $6,000 over weekends with friends, in black and white.
Christopher Nolan films by release.Memento: The story runs backward in color and forward in black and white, based on his brother Jonathan's short story.
Christopher Nolan films by release.Insomnia: A remake of a Norwegian thriller, it was set in Alaska but filmed in British Columbia.
Christopher Nolan films by release.Batman Begins: The reboot's Tumbler Batmobile was a real working vehicle built for the film.
Christopher Nolan films by release.The Prestige: Two rival magicians, with David Bowie playing Nikola Tesla.
Christopher Nolan films by release.The Dark Knight: Heath Ledger won a posthumous Oscar, and it was the first fiction feature shot partly with IMAX cameras.
Christopher Nolan films by release.Inception: Nolan spent roughly ten years on the script, and the spinning top ending is still debated.
Christopher Nolan films by release.Interstellar: Physicist Kip Thorne advised, and the Gargantua black hole visuals led to real scientific papers.
Christopher Nolan films by release.Dunkirk: Real ships and thousands of extras rather than computer graphics, told in three interwoven timelines.
Christopher Nolan films by release.Oppenheimer: It won seven Oscars including Best Picture and Best Director, with the Trinity test shown without CGI.

When these snacks first appeared.Oreo: Nabisco has never said where the name came from; it became America's best-selling cookie.
When these snacks first appeared.Cheez-It: The crackers began in Dayton, Ohio, and the cheese is baked right in.
When these snacks first appeared.Twinkies: James Dewar's creation first had banana cream, but a wartime banana shortage pushed the maker to switch to vanilla.
When these snacks first appeared.Ritz crackers: Launched during the Great Depression, its name lent an air of luxury to an affordable cracker.
When these snacks first appeared.Cheetos: Frito-Lay's puffed snack gained a mascot in 1986, Chester Cheetah.
When these snacks first appeared.Goldfish crackers (US): Margaret Rudkin of Pepperidge Farm discovered the cracker on a trip to Switzerland, and brought it to America.
When these snacks first appeared.Pop-Tarts: Kellogg's rushed them out to beat a rival product from Post, and the name nodded to pop art.
When these snacks first appeared.Pringles: Chemist Fredric Baur designed its stackable can and was reportedly buried partly in one.
When these snacks first appeared.Hot Pockets: Brothers Paul and David Merage, who came from Iran, developed the microwave sleeve that makes the crust crisp.
When these snacks first appeared.Takis: This Mexican brand's rolled tortilla chips are named after the taquito, and their intense flavour is the whole selling point.

Non-Disney animated films by release.The Secret of NIMH: Don Bluth's film about a widowed mouse was based on a children's book whose heroine was renamed to avoid a toy brand. NIMH is a lab.
Non-Disney animated films by release.An American Tail: Fievel Mouskewitz, a young immigrant mouse, got a hit song called "Somewhere Out There." Steven Spielberg was involved in the film.
Non-Disney animated films by release.The Land Before Time: Littlefoot the baby dinosaur lost his mother in this tearjerker. The film spawned over a dozen straight-to-video sequels.
Non-Disney animated films by release.FernGully: This environmental fable about rainforest fairies featured Robin Williams as the manic bat Batty Koda. Much of his role was improvised.
Non-Disney animated films by release.Anastasia: This film mixed the Russian Romanov legend with magic. In real life, DNA tests later showed Anastasia did not survive 1918.
Non-Disney animated films by release.The Iron Giant: Brad Bird directed this tale of a boy and a robot that fell from space. It flopped at first, then became a beloved classic.
Non-Disney animated films by release.Despicable Me: Illumination's first Despicable Me film introduced Gru and the Minions. The Minions' gibberish was voiced by co-director Pierre Coffin.
Non-Disney animated films by release.The LEGO Movie: Everything in this film is made of bricks, and its song "Everything Is Awesome" became hugely popular. It was written by Phil Lord and Christopher Miller.
Non-Disney animated films by release.Sing: A koala theatre owner puts on a singing contest for animals in this film. Many of the songs are well-known pop hits.
Non-Disney animated films by release.KPop Demon Hunters: This Netflix film follows a K-pop girl group that secretly fights demons. Its song "Golden" became a worldwide chart-topper.

Pets on the scale.Betta fish: Bettas breathe air from the surface using a special organ. Males guard bubble nests, and fight each other if kept together.
Pets on the scale.Budgerigar: Budgies are native to Australia, and wild ones are always green. Some pet ones learn hundreds of words.
Pets on the scale.Syrian hamster: Almost all pet Syrian hamsters descend from a few found in Syria in 1930. They store food in cheek pouches that stretch to their shoulders.
Pets on the scale.Fancy rat: Pet rats are social and clever, and they "laugh" at ultrasonic pitches when tickled. They can learn tricks like dogs.
Pets on the scale.Guinea pig: Guinea pigs aren't from Guinea and aren't pigs. They come from the Andes, and like us, can't make their own vitamin C.
Pets on the scale.Pet rabbit: A rabbit's teeth never stop growing, so it must keep chewing. Happy ones leap and twist in what's called a binky.
Pets on the scale.House cat: Cats sleep for 12 to 16 hours a day. Their purring is thought to help bone and tissue healing.
Pets on the scale.Beagle: A beagle has about 220 million scent receptors, compared to about 5 million in a person. That's why they're used at airports.
Pets on the scale.Golden retriever: They are favourites as guide and therapy dogs because of their gentle manner. Their coats are water-repellent.
Pets on the scale.Great Dane: Despite the name, the breed is German, not Danish. The tallest dog ever recorded, Zeus, stood over a metre at the shoulder.

How many live together in one group?.Tiger (usually alone): Tigers hunt and live alone, except for mothers with cubs. Each adult patrols a large territory and marks it with scent and scratches.
How many live together in one group?.Swans (a mated pair): Swans often form lifelong pairs, and the male is called a cob and the female a pen. They are known to defend their nest fiercely.
How many live together in one group?.Wolf pack: A pack is generally a family, with a breeding pair and their offspring. Cooperation lets wolves take prey far larger than any one of them.
How many live together in one group?.Lion pride: A pride is built around related females and their cubs, with a few males. Lionesses often synchronise births so cubs can be raised together.
How many live together in one group?.Naked mole-rat colony: Only one queen breeds in the colony, which is rare for a mammal. The other members dig tunnels, forage and defend the nest.
How many live together in one group?.Garden ant nest: Many workers are sisters, all daughters of the queen. Black garden ants are famous for farming aphids and milking them for sugary honeydew.
How many live together in one group?.Honeybee hive: A summer hive can hold tens of thousands of bees, but only one queen. Workers communicate food sources with a waggle dance.
How many live together in one group?.Wildebeest migration: The great herd circles between Tanzania's Serengeti and Kenya's Maasai Mara, following the rains, and faces crocodiles at river crossings.
How many live together in one group?.Leafcutter ant colony: These ants don't eat the leaves they carry; they use them to grow a fungus underground. A large colony is a city with millions of workers.
How many live together in one group?.Bracken Cave bat colony: Near San Antonio, Texas, this cave holds the biggest bat colony on Earth, of Mexican free-tailed bats. They emerge at dusk to eat tonnes of insects.

A frog's life, step by step.Frog lays frogspawn: A common frog can lay up to 2,000 eggs in a clump of jelly. The jelly protects the eggs and swells in the water.
A frog's life, step by step.Black dots grow in the jelly: Each dark dot is an embryo developing in its jelly capsule. Warmth speeds it up, and eggs hatch in a few weeks.
A frog's life, step by step.Tadpoles wriggle free: Newly hatched tadpoles have gills and cling to plants. They have no legs yet and breathe like a fish.
A frog's life, step by step.Tadpoles nibble algae: Most tadpoles are mainly vegetarian at first, scraping algae from plants. Later they may eat small animals.
A frog's life, step by step.Back legs appear: The hind legs start as tiny buds and then grow quickly. By now the tadpole has developed lungs as well as gills.
A frog's life, step by step.Front legs pop out: The front legs develop hidden under a skin flap and then emerge all at once. The young frog now begins to look like an adult.
A frog's life, step by step.Tail shrinks away: The tail isn't dropped; the body absorbs it and uses it as food. This is part of the metamorphosis, which takes about 14 weeks.
A frog's life, step by step.Froglet hops onto land: Tiny froglets leave the pond in large numbers, often after rain. Many are eaten by birds, snakes and other predators.
A frog's life, step by step.Grows into an adult frog: Frogs absorb water and oxygen through their skin. They moult regularly, and often eat their own shed skin.
A frog's life, step by step.Returns to the pond to breed: Males call to attract females, and they inflate a vocal sac to make it louder. Frogs often return to the very pond where they hatched.

Rumpelstiltskin, in story order.Miller boasts about his girl: The Grimms published Rumpelstiltskin in 1812; a similar British tale, Tom Tit Tot, has a spinning imp too.
Rumpelstiltskin, in story order.King locks her in with straw: Gold thread was real: thin strips of gold were wound around silk or other fibre to make luxurious fabric.
Rumpelstiltskin, in story order.Spun for her necklace: Spinning wheels spread across Europe in the Middle Ages, so a girl forced to spin was a very familiar image.
Rumpelstiltskin, in story order.Spun again for her ring: In German he is Rumpelstilzchen, a name linked to a type of rattling, poltergeist-like spirit.
Rumpelstiltskin, in story order.She promises her firstborn: Bargaining a child to a supernatural being is a classic fairy-tale danger, and the name-guessing escape clause makes the deal beatable.
Rumpelstiltskin, in story order.She marries the king: The miller's lie wins his daughter a crown, in a tale that is oddly blunt about fortune coming from deceit.
Rumpelstiltskin, in story order.The queen's baby is born: The imp's return when the baby is born is a harsh twist in a story that began with a father's boast.
Rumpelstiltskin, in story order.Three days to guess his name: Guessing a creature's true name to break its power is a worldwide folklore motif, from fairy tales to ancient magic.
Rumpelstiltskin, in story order.A messenger hears him sing: In the Grimms' tale the messenger sees the imp dancing around a fire, singing Today I bake, tomorrow I brew.
Rumpelstiltskin, in story order.\"Rumpelstiltskin!\": In the Grimms' tale he stamps so hard he sinks through the ground, while a later edition has him tear himself in two.

Thanksgiving traditions, by when they be.Plymouth harvest feast: Records mention wildfowl and five deer at the three-day feast with the Wampanoag, though nothing says the main dish was turkey.
Thanksgiving traditions, by when they be.Lincoln's proclamation: He declared a national day of thanks in the middle of the Civil War, after editor Sarah Josepha Hale, who also wrote Mary Had a Little Lamb, lobbied for years.
Thanksgiving traditions, by when they be.Macy's parade: It began with live animals borrowed from the Central Park Zoo; giant balloons replaced them in 1927, starting with Felix the Cat.
Thanksgiving traditions, by when they be.Detroit Lions game: The football game was created to draw crowds to a struggling team, and it has been played nearly every year since.
Thanksgiving traditions, by when they be.Fourth-Thursday law: Congress fixed the holiday after Franklin Roosevelt's move to an earlier Thursday split the country and confused calendars and retailers.
Thanksgiving traditions, by when they be.Swanson TV dinner: Legend says the trays were invented to use up a huge surplus of leftover frozen turkey, and early dinners were turkey with cornbread dressing.
Thanksgiving traditions, by when they be.Cowboys' first game: The team, founded in 1960, started playing on Thanksgiving in 1966 and has hosted a game on the day almost every year since.
Thanksgiving traditions, by when they be.Charlie Brown special: It features the infamous meal of toast, popcorn and jelly beans, and it is one of several holiday specials by Charles Schulz and Bill Melendez.
Thanksgiving traditions, by when they be.Butterball hotline: The Turkey Talk-Line started with a handful of staffers answering calls about thawing and roasting a bird, and it grew into a national lifeline.
Thanksgiving traditions, by when they be.Official turkey pardon: George H.W. Bush made the pardon an official ritual, though earlier presidents had received turkeys; the birds now retire to a farm.
